snap_deductions.item: FY2026 standard deduction, 48 states + DC, household of 1 (1-3 persons)
snap_deductions.publisher: California Department of Social Services, ACIN I-46-25 (relaying the USDA FNS FY2026 COLA)
snap_deductions.note: Same $209 read in NY OTDA GIS 25DC059 and CT DSS Program Standards Chart. Effective 1 Oct 2025 - 30 Sep 2026. FNS memo itself (usda.gov/.../fns.snap-cola-fy26memo.pdf) returned 403.

snap_deductions.item: FY2026 maximum excess shelter deduction, 48 states + DC
snap_deductions.publisher: California Department of Social Services, ACIN I-46-25
snap_deductions.note: Cap applies to households without an elderly or disabled member (those are uncapped). Also read in OTDA GIS 25DC059.

snap_deductions.publisher: California Department of Social Services, ACIN I-46-25

snap_deductions.item: FY2027 standard deduction, 48 states + DC, household 1-3
snap_deductions.note: Figure from search-engine excerpt of the official memo; the PDF itself returned 403 to both WebFetch and curl. Effective 1 Oct 2026.

snap_deductions.item: FY2027 maximum excess shelter deduction, 48 states + DC
snap_deductions.note: Search excerpt only (403 on the PDF). Same excerpt: homeless shelter deduction $205.66; elderly/disabled asset limit $4,750.
Quoted: 'a deduction of 20 percent of all earned income to compensate for taxes, other mandatory deductions from salary, and work expenses.'

snap_deductions.figure: Shelter costs minus 50% of monthly income after all other deductions; capped at the shelter cap unless an elderly/disabled member
snap_deductions.note: Quoted: deduction 'to the extent that the monthly amount expended by a household for shelter exceeds an amount equal to 50 percent of monthly household income after all other applicable deductions have been allowed.' Order: gross income -> minus 20% earned income -> minus standard deduction -> minus dependent care, medical (elderly/disabled over $35), child support -> = adjusted income; excess shelter = (rent/mortgage + SUA) - 0.5 x adjusted income, capped; net income = adjusted - excess shelter.

snap_deductions.item: SUA, New York City, FY2026 (Heating/AC SUA)
snap_deductions.publisher: NYS OTDA GIS 25DC059 (copy hosted by Warren County; original otda.ny.gov/policy/gis/2025/25DC059.pdf reset the connection)
snap_deductions.note: NY SUAs do not vary by household size. Amounts include water, sewage and trash.

snap_deductions.item: SUA, Rest of New York State, FY2026

snap_deductions.publisher: California Department of Social Services, ACIN I-46-25
snap_deductions.note: Statewide, not by household size. SUA requires heating/cooling costs separate from rent; LUA = two or more non-heating utilities; TUA = phone only.
Same chart lists Max Shelter $744, Homeless $198.99, standard deduction $209 for 1-3 persons, confirming these are the FY2026 SNAP values.

snap_deductions.item: OBBBA 2025 Sec. 10104: internet costs excluded from shelter
snap_deductions.figure: Internet service fees may not be counted toward the excess shelter deduction (nor folded into a SUA)
snap_deductions.note: Quoted: 'Any service fee associated with internet connection shall not be used in computing the excess shelter expense deduction under this paragraph.' FNS Q&A memo of 8 May 2026 (usda.gov) on implementation was not fetchable.

snap_deductions.item: OBBBA 2025 Sec. 10103: LIHEAP 'Heat and Eat' limited
snap_deductions.figure: Automatic heating/cooling SUA via a LIHEAP payment now only for households with an elderly or disabled member
snap_deductions.publisher: Connecticut DSS presentation 'DSS Benefits and H.R. 1'
snap_deductions.note: Quoted: 'Limits the SNAP-LIHEAP connection (known as Heat & Eat), to only apply to households with an elderly or disabled member.' Effective upon passage (Sec. 10103). Other households must show actual heating/cooling costs to get the HCSUA.

medi_cal_state_funded.figure: From 1 Jan 2026, new applicants aged 19+, not pregnant, with no immigration status, unverified status, or certain non-immigrant visas get restricted-scope (emergency/pregnancy) Medi-Cal only
medi_cal_state_funded.publisher: Marin County HHS, 'Expansion Freeze Questions and Answers' (county relay of DHCS guidance, ACWDL 25-13)
medi_cal_state_funded.note: DHCS's own ACWDL 25-13 (dhcs.ca.gov/.../25-13.pdf, 30 Jun 2025) not readable (Incapsula). Existing enrollees keep full scope; a three-month grace period lets them re-enroll after a discontinuance. Pregnant people exempt through 365 days postpartum.

medi_cal_state_funded.figure: $30/month, ages 19-59, effective no sooner than 1 July 2027
medi_cal_state_funded.note: Applies to new and current members with UIS, NQIs under the 5-year bar, and PRUCOL claimants. Not income-based; no household cap; each member charged. After no more than 90 days' nonpayment, moved to restricted scope. Exempt: pregnant, 60+, 18 and under, restricted-scope members. Authority: AB 116 (2025), W&I Code 14007.8.

medi_cal_state_funded.figure: Non-emergency dental removed from 1 July 2026 ('Full Scope with no Dental') for UIS adults 19+ not pregnant
medi_cal_state_funded.note: Emergency dental still covered. Pregnant members keep full scope with dental.

medi_cal_state_funded.figure: Status not in a category accepted for federal full-scope Medicaid, or not verified
medi_cal_state_funded.note: Quoted: UIS means 'their current immigration situation does not meet the requirements for full federal eligibility, either because their status is not one of the accepted categories or because it has not yet been verified.' SIS = qualified immigrants (after 5-year bar or exempt) and lawfully present immigrants under 21 or pregnant.

medi_cal_state_funded.item: Which non-immigrant visas the freeze covers; O-1 treatment
medi_cal_state_funded.figure: Student, work and visitor/tourist visas are covered by the freeze; U and T visas are not
medi_cal_state_funded.publisher: Health Consumer Alliance practice tip (legal-services advocates; not DHCS)
medi_cal_state_funded.note: Quoted: 'only the student, work, and visitor/tourist visas are included here, and not other non-immigrant visas like U or T visas.' An O-1 is a temporary work visa: a lawfully present O-1 adult aged 21+ (not pregnant) has UIS for Medi-Cal, so a new application from 1 Jan 2026 gets restricted scope only. If enrolled before 2026 they keep full scope with no dental and, at 19-59, will owe the $30 premium from July 2027. DHCS does not name O-1 by name in the pages read; this is derived from the advocates' reading of W&I Code 14007.8(b)(1).

medi_cal_state_funded.figure: NY residents, lawfully present, aged 19-64, not eligible for Medicaid/CHP or employer coverage; income up to $31,920 for 1 person (200% FPL) from 1 July 2026
medi_cal_state_funded.note: $0 premium, no deductible; dental and vision included. Cost sharing: $0 below $23,940; $15 PCP / $25 specialist / $150 inpatient / $75 ER for $23,941-$31,920. A lawfully present O-1 holder qualifies if income-eligible.

medi_cal_state_funded.figure: Income limit cut from 250% to 200% FPL on 1 July 2026; ~450,000 enrollees ($31,920-$39,900) lost eligibility
medi_cal_state_funded.publisher: NY State of Health fact sheet
medi_cal_state_funded.note: No change for the 1.3 million enrollees below 200% FPL. DACA recipients at or below 138% FPL moved to Medicaid on 1 July 2026; higher-income non-pregnant DACA recipients no longer qualify for any NYSOH program. Pregnant enrollees stay covered. Program reverted from Section 1332 waiver to Section 1331 Basic Health Program (CMS approval 23 Mar 2026, per nyhealthaccess.org/entry/252).

building_permits.item: Los Angeles (LADBS) building permit fee, LAMC 91.113 Table 1-A
building_permits.publisher: LA Dept of City Planning, Housing Element 2021-2029 Appendix 2.4 (reproducing LADBS Table 1-A, effective 16 July 2018)
building_permits.note: Bracket boundaries re-aligned from a broken PDF column layout; the over-$1,000,000 row was not shown. Plan check = 90% of the building permit fee (LAMC 91.107.3.1.1). Many surcharges stack on top: the city's own samples give a 1,200 sq ft new ADU at $121,200 valuation a total permit cost of $8,447.62, and a $20,000 garage conversion $1,045.22. Valuation is set by LADBS's Building Permit Valuation Table (effective 17 Aug 2015) at dbs.lacity.gov/faq/fee-schedules. LAMC on amlegal was 403, so a later index adjustment can't be ruled out.

building_permits.item: New York City new building work permit, 1-, 2- or 3-family dwelling
building_permits.figure: $0.06 per sq ft of total floor area, minimum $100 per structure
building_permits.publisher: NYC DOB Service Update, Local Law 56 of 2016 (Admin Code 28-112.2)
building_permits.note: Permit fees sit in Admin Code §28-112.2, not 1 RCNY 101-03. The 101-03 PDF (read) covers miscellaneous DOB fees such as CO copies at $5, periodic inspections at $65 and variance requests at $1,000. Other new buildings under 7 storeys and 100,000 sq ft pay $0.26/sq ft with a $280 minimum; 7+ storeys or over 100,000 sq ft pay $0.45/sq ft with a $290 minimum. I could not read the current text of §28-112.2 (amlegal and iccsafe both returned 403).

building_permits.item: New York City alteration permit (kitchen/bath remodel), 1-, 2- or 3-family dwelling
building_permits.figure: Minimum filing fee for first $5,000 of cost (Alt-1 $170; Alt-2, Alt-3, Limited Alteration $130) + $2.60 per $1,000 (or fraction) of cost above $5,000
building_permits.note: Rate cut from $5.15 to $2.60 per $1,000. Other buildings under 7 storeys pay a minimum fee for the first $3,000 (Alt-1 $280; Alt-2 $225; Alt-3 and LAA $195) plus $10.30 per $1,000 above $3,000. Example: a $30,000 Alt-2 kitchen in a one-family house = $130 + 25 x $2.60 = $195 (rule-derived).

building_permits.item: New Haven, CT building permit fee
building_permits.figure: $25 for first $1,000 of value + $15 per additional $1,000, plus $10 processing fee (reported)
building_permits.note: newhavenct.gov Building Department pages returned 403, so this wasn't verified on a city page. The Connecticut state education fee (CGS 29-252a) also applies but wasn't sourced in this sweep.

hamble_drive.item: Road distance, central London (Charing Cross) to Hamble-le-Rice (Hamble Lane)
hamble_drive.figure: 139.2 km (86.5 miles), about 1 h 54 min free-flow
hamble_drive.publisher: OSRM public routing engine on OpenStreetMap data (computed for this sweep)
hamble_drive.note: This is a routing calculation, not a published figure. The AA route planner is a JavaScript app and couldn't be fetched. Route is via the M3 and M27, or the A3/A27.
Not read on the page. Rome2rio's 'London' origin point is probably not Charing Cross, which would explain the ~4-mile gap from OSRM. Recommend ~83-87 miles / 135-140 km.
